title: Reduce community malaria transmission through vaccination

concept.text: Vaccinate infectious human populations to reduce onward transmission and incident infections in the community. Pfs230D1 clinical studies demonstrate functional transmission-blocking signals, but these are not yet proof of community-level protection. Proposed completion test: WHO recommendation for transmission reduction, supported by a cluster-randomized endemic-area trial showing fewer incident human infections over at least two transmission seasons, with a prespecified efficacy confidence interval excluding no benefit. Test set by: WHO PPC: 'reduction of incident human infections at the community level.' Cluster design, two-season duration and statistical boundary are proposed operational criteria. Overlaps: INF-04, INF-13. Sources given: [WHO transmission-reducing vaccine PPC](https://www.who.int/tools/target-product-profile-database/item/ppc--for-vaccines-to-reduce-malaria-transmission) ; [Primary Pfs230D1 clinical trial publication](https://media.malariaworld.org/A_Vaccine_to_Block_Plasmodium_falciparum_Transmission_b57ee04012.pdf).

page.title: Malaria transmission-blocking vaccines
page.definition: Vaccination induces antibodies that inhibit malaria-parasite development in mosquitoes and thereby reduces new human infections at community level. Mosquitoes ingest the antibodies when they feed on vaccinated people.

goal.need: Malaria cases increased by approximately 9 million between 2023 and 2024. CDC identifies vaccines that reduce transmission and human infection as a route to elimination through mass vaccination.

figures.note: WHO estimates; cases are episodes, not necessarily distinct people.

statements.body: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
statements.quote: Develop malaria vaccines that reduce transmission and human malaria infection, enabling elimination in multiple settings through mass vaccination campaigns.
statements.context: A strategic goal of the Malaria Vaccine Technology Roadmap, reproduced by CDC.

statements.quote: However, if malaria vaccines are to contribute to programs for malaria elimination, they will need to have an impact on malaria transmission.
Establish the safety and efficacy of a Pfs230D1+ R21 combination vaccine.
statements.context: An objective of PfVIMT, which began on 1 March 2025.

completion.title: Vaccination reduces incident human malaria infections by reducing transmission at community level.
completion.criterion: Demonstrate a vaccine-attributable reduction in incident human malaria infections at community level. WHO recognises phase 3 cluster-randomised studies and postlicensure community-effectiveness studies. Its preferred product characteristics specify no universal numerical efficacy target, minimum follow-up duration or vaccination-coverage threshold.
completion.set_by: WHO, 2022 preferred product characteristics, section 2.3 and clinical-development guidance.
completion.threshold_quote: The vaccine should reduce malaria transmission, resulting in the reduction of incident human infections at the community level.
completion.basis: This is WHO's stated public-health endpoint. Mosquito-feeding activity alone does not establish fewer human infections. WHO allows a surrogate-based approval pathway but calls for subsequent community-effectiveness evaluation.

milestones.title: A malaria vaccine induces animal antibodies that reduce mosquito oocyst development by at least 80%.
milestones.criterion: Animal antisera reduce mean mosquito oocyst counts by at least 80% versus control in membrane-feeding assays; oocysts are parasite cysts in the mosquito gut. This is a screening benchmark at a stated antibody concentration. Published on 8 August 2007, Pfs25 studies used 8 rabbits and Pvs25 studies 10 rhesus macaques. Fitted 80% inhibition occurred at approximately 2,800 and 6,000 antigen-specific ELISA units, respectively; these assay-specific units do not establish community protection.
milestones.set_by: Transmission-blocking vaccine research convention, stated as a functional benchmark by Bender et al. (2021) and used in Pfs25/Pvs25 assay studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: antibodies against a TBV candidate should block ≥80% of Plasmodium oocyst development

milestones.title: A malaria vaccine demonstrates tolerability and induces functional antibodies in a phase 1 human study.
milestones.criterion: A phase 1 study establishes tolerability and antibodies that inhibit parasite development in mosquito membrane-feeding assays. P. falciparum: Pfs230D1-EPA/AS01 produced functional activity lasting about 1 year after dose 3, with no serious adverse events among 117 vaccine recipients in a 236-person main cohort. P. vivax: Pvs25H/Alhydrogel, published on 2 May 2005, induced functional antibodies in a trial of 30 adults, with no vaccine-related serious adverse events.
milestones.set_by: UNDP/World Bank/WHO TDR expert meeting report (2000), section B.3, phase I definition; applies to both parasite species.
milestones.threshold_quote: safety and immunogenicity in naive or target populations

milestones.title: Vaccination reduces malaria transmission from naturally infected people to mosquitoes.
milestones.criterion: A controlled direct-feeding study demonstrates reduced mosquito infection after feeding on naturally infected vaccinees. P. falciparum: results published on 24 June 2025 included 236 injected adults: 56 full-dose, 61 fractional-dose and 119 controls. The primary efficacy analysis combining regimens over 6 weeks did not demonstrate efficacy. A secondary full-dose analysis found 72.5% fewer positive feeds over two seasons (95% CI 30.4–89.1%). This is a secondary efficacy signal. No qualifying P. vivax result was identified.
milestones.set_by: UNDP/World Bank/WHO TDR expert meeting report (2000), section B.3, phase II definition; applies to both parasite species.
milestones.threshold_quote: block the transmission of malaria from naturally infected vaccinees to mosquitos by direct feed.

milestones.title: A malaria vaccine confirms safety and mosquito efficacy in a multicountry phase 3 trial at ages ≥5 years.
milestones.criterion: A multicountry phase 3 trial in participants aged 5 years and older confirms safety and efficacy against mosquito transmission using direct skin feeding assays. The published PfVIMT design concerns Pfs230D1+R21 against P. falciparum. No qualifying phase 3 result was identified for either parasite species.
milestones.set_by: Global Health EDCTP3, PfVIMT project description; this published design and age threshold were specified for the P. falciparum combination vaccine.
milestones.threshold_quote: using the direct skin feeding assay to assess its impact on transmission.

milestones.title: A regulator approves a malaria vaccine for transmission reduction using a validated surrogate endpoint.
milestones.criterion: A regulator grants accelerated approval based on a validated surrogate endpoint for reduced human transmission, conditional on establishing effectiveness after approval. WHO presents this as an alternative to a phase 3 community trial. No qualifying approval was identified for either parasite species.
milestones.set_by: WHO, 2022 clinical-development guidance, Figure 2; the pathway and conditions are stated in a figure.

not_found: No published community-incidence efficacy result for a transmission-blocking malaria vaccine was identified for either parasite species through 15 November 2026.
No controlled direct-feeding efficacy result in naturally infected P. vivax vaccine recipients was identified.
No completed multicountry phase 3 efficacy result or surrogate-based regulatory approval was identified for either parasite species.

results.finding: STAC-immunized mice (n=6): purified IgG reduced P. falciparum mosquito oocyst density by >98%.
results.detail: Standard membrane-feeding assay used purified IgG at 75 µg/mL. The reported result is a laboratory screening measure, not community protection.
results.quote: When the IgGs were tested at 75 µg/mL, the combination, Pfs230-D1, and STAC groups showed almost complete inhibition (>98% inhibition), while Pfs48/45-D3 alone IgG showed 73% inhibition (Fig.

results.finding: Pvs25 mRNA-vaccinated mice (n=6 per group): antisera reduced mean P. vivax oocyst counts by 100%.
results.detail: Pooled sera were tested at 1:2 dilution in a direct membrane-feeding assay, with reduction measured against a human AB-serum control.
results.quote:
In contrast to the sera from control
animals that enhanced the oocyst number by ~1.7-fold, all
samples from Pvs25 mRNA –LNP-immunized mice exhibited
complete (100%) transmission-blocking activity at 1:2 dilution.

results.finding: Pfs230D1-EPA/AS01 phase 1: 117 vaccine recipients; functional activity persisted about 1 year after dose 3.
results.detail: The main cohort included 236 participants. No serious adverse events occurred among vaccine recipients. The primary direct skin-feeding efficacy analysis did not demonstrate reduced transmission during the first six weeks.

results.finding: Pvs25H/Alhydrogel induced functional antibodies in a phase 1 trial of 30 adults, with 0 vaccine-related serious adverse events.
results.detail: Sera from 27 vaccinees were assessed in membrane-feeding experiments. The five sera with the highest antibody levels after dose 3 reduced the number of infected mosquitoes by 20–30%.
results.quote: Vaccine-induced antibody is functionally active as evidenced by significant transmission blocking activity in the membrane feeding assay.

results.finding: P. falciparum vaccine trial: 236 adults were injected; full-dose recipients had 72.5% fewer positive mosquito feeds over two seasons.
results.detail: The randomized controlled study used direct skin feeding. The combined-regimen primary efficacy analysis over six weeks did not demonstrate efficacy. The full-dose finding was a secondary signal; its 95% CI was 30.4% to 89.1%, without adjustment for multiplicity.
